content.user_title: Build a Data Supply-Demand Matching System
content.value_statement: Unstructured demand and resource records make reliable matching slow and inconsistent. This skill provides database designs, matching states, operating procedures, and review checks.
actual_capabilities: Designs field structures for data resource, demand, and expert service databases.
Validates demand records using identified buyers, defined purposes, and stated budgets.
Classifies opportunities into direct, processed, combined, external, or future-development matching states.
Creates matching plans, tracking records, update logs, and supply-demand analysis outlines.
Recommends tags, maintenance schedules, and tool choices based on database size.
Applies quality checks for ownership, tradability, qualifications, freshness, and record completeness.
limitations: It does not access live marketplaces, customer systems, or private databases.
It cannot verify ownership, qualifications, prices, or buyer claims without supplied evidence.
Its matching efficiency formula is a planning model, not a validated prediction algorithm.
It does not provide legal, regulatory, licensing, or transaction approval.

use_cases.title: Structure an Early Data Marketplace
use_cases.description: Define three connected databases, practical fields, tags, and an operating sequence for a new matching program.

use_cases.title: Assess a New Buyer Request
use_cases.description: Check demand completeness, assign a matching state, and identify the next action and missing evidence.

use_cases.title: Review Portfolio Gaps
use_cases.description: Analyze unmatched demand and stale records to prioritize resource acquisition and database maintenance.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Demand Record
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this demand record: [record]. Check buyer identity, purpose, budget, timing, and decision chain. List missing fields and propose clarifying questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner validation of a single request

prompt_templates.title: Design the Three Databases
prompt_templates.prompt: Design resource, demand, and expert databases for [organization]. Provide fields, definitions, required status, tags, update owners, and maintenance frequency.

prompt_templates.title: Classify and Plan a Match
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this demand [details] with these resources [details]. Assign matching state A-E, explain evidence, identify compliance gates, and create an action plan.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Matching Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these demand, resource, expert, and outcome records: [records]. Measure coverage, precision, outcomes, aging, and gaps. Recommend quarterly priorities with assumptions.

output_examples.input: A hospital needs monthly regional disease statistics within six weeks. The budget and decision owner are unknown.
output_examples.output: Demand status: incomplete. The buyer and purpose are identifiable, but budget and decision authority need confirmation before matching. Ask who approves procurement, the budget range, required fields, geographic scope, permitted uses, and privacy constraints.

output_examples.input: A buyer needs a combined mobility and retail dataset. Separate compliant sources are available, but no combined product exists.
output_examples.output: Matching state: C, combined match. Confirm each source's ownership and tradability, define join keys and permitted processing, assess privacy risk, estimate integration work, and record supplier responsibilities before introduction.

output_examples.input: Review a database with 140 demand records, many duplicates, and no update history.
output: Adopt a lightweight CRM or searchable database because record volume exceeds the spreadsheet guideline.
Define unique record identifiers, duplicate rules, owners, status values, and monthly review dates.
Archive expired demand, preserve outcome reasons, and publish a monthly update log.
Use unmatched valid demand to guide new resource acquisition.

best_practices: Record evidence, assumptions, ownership status, and permitted uses before recommending a match.
Prioritize complete demand records, then acquire resources that address verified unmet demand.
Review records monthly and analyze outcomes quarterly using consistent statuses and reasons.
anti_patterns: Do not treat vague interest without a buyer, purpose, and budget as validated demand.
Do not recommend introductions before checking ownership, tradability, confidentiality, and qualification requirements.
Do not build a complex platform before record volume and workflow needs justify it.

faq.question: Which database should I build first?
faq.answer: Start with the demand database. Verified demand determines which resources and expert services should be collected.

faq.question: What makes a demand record valid?
faq.answer: Identify a real buyer, a clear use, and a budget or budget range. Also capture timing and decision authority.

faq.question: What do matching states A through E mean?
faq.answer: They represent direct, processed, combined, external, and future-development matches. Each state leads to a different next action.

faq.question: When should I replace spreadsheets?
faq.answer: The knowledge base suggests considering a lightweight CRM or custom system after approximately 100 records.

faq.question: Does the skill contact suppliers or buyers?
faq.answer: No. It prepares structures, assessments, plans, and tracking records from information you provide.

faq.question: Can this skill approve a data transaction?
faq.answer: No. Qualified legal, compliance, security, and transaction professionals must verify requirements and authorize decisions.
